Modulo \(8\): since \(1978\equiv 2\pmod 8\),
\[
1978^m-1978^n=1978^n(1978^k-1)\equiv 2^n(2^k-1)\pmod 8.
\]
Since \(2^k-1\) is odd, divisibility by \(8\) requires \(n\ge 3\).

Modulo \(125\): \(\gcd(1978,125)=1\), so \(1978^n\) is invertible. Thus we need
\[
1978^k\equiv 1\pmod{125}.
\]
Now \(1978\equiv -22\pmod{125}\). Compute
\[
22^2\equiv -16,\quad 22^4\equiv 6,\quad 22^5\equiv 7,\quad 22^{10}\equiv 49,\quad 22^{20}\equiv 26,\quad 22^{50}\equiv -1.
\]
Hence \(22^{100}\equiv 1\pmod{125}\), and the order of \(-22\) modulo \(125\) is \(100\). Therefore the minimal \(k=m-n\) is \(100\).

So \(m=n+100\), and
\[
m+n=2n+100.
\]
Minimizing with \(n\ge 3\) gives \(n=3\), so \(m=103\).

\[
\boxed{106}
\]
